metadata.case_name: CHEUNG YUK CHUN AND OTHERS v. MITSUI CONSTRUCION CO LTD AND ANOTHER [1984]

source: YUK CHUN suffered a fracture of the right humerus, a bone of the upper arm, and received a de-gloving injury of both legs and feet. She underwent immediate treatment to her legs and the arm was put in plaster. On 8th October 1981 the fractured humerus was the subject of an operation when a bone plate and screws were applied. I am told that these were subsequently removed in a further operation about a year after and there is no functional disability remaining as a result.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of shoulder or upper arm, unspecified

injuries.description: de-gloving injury of both legs and feet
source: YUK CHUN suffered a fracture of the right humerus, a bone of the upper arm, and received a de-gloving injury of both legs and feet.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified open wound of ankle or foot

injuries.description: scar on the back of the upper arm
source: In late October and mid-November 1981 skin grafts were carried out to both legs and feet using skin from both thighs. She also has a scar on the back of the upper arm.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified superficial injury of shoulder or upper arm

injuries.description: functional disability: cannot straighten her left foot; walks on tip-toe with spine and pelvis tilted to compensate
source: She has been left with substantial scarring over both legs and both feet. She has also suffered a functional disability in that she cannot straighten her left foot. She must walk on tip-toe with her spine and pelvis tilted to compensate for this.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of other specified muscle, fascia or tendon at ankle or foot level

injuries.description: keloid formation of scars on ankles, calves and thighs
source: After her discharge from hospital the scars on both legs and feet and on her arm attracted some keloid formation which is an overgrowth of the skin projecting the scar beyond skin level and is extremely ugly in appearance. This formed on the ankles, calves and thighs, the latter having been the donor area for the skin grafts performed while she was in hospital.

manifestations.description: Extensive and unsightly scarring on both legs and feet
Keloid formation of scars (proj ecting scar beyond skin level) on ankles, calves and thighs
Cannot straighten her left foot; must walk on tip-toe with spine and pelvis tilted to compensate
Permanent limp (will always walk with a limp and be unable to disguise it)
Scar on the back of the upper arm

treatments_received: Operation on fractured humerus with bone plate and screws on 8th October 1981
Skin grafts to both legs and feet in late October and mid-November 1981 using skin from both thighs
Removal of bone plate and screws in a further operation about a year after
treatments_future: Lengthening of the Achilles tendon (to improve movement of left foot), estimated hospitalisation 4 days
Flap graft to replace the whole of the scar on the left foot (tube graft), both legs plastered together for 3-4 weeks, total hospitalisation about 10 weeks
Future treatment likely to be carried out in Glasgow; private treatment estimated by Dr. Wedderburn at £5,000 (judge allowed $50,000)

losses.description: Extensive and unsightly scarring on both legs and feet with keloid formation; cosmetic disability and psychological reluctance to be seen in bathing suit, skirt or shorts; will substantially hamper general enjoyment of life

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Permanent functional disability and limp will considerably limit her ability to play sport and indulge in prolonged activity requiring walking or running
Scarring implications will become more serious as she grows older and particularly as she reaches the age of marriage
Permanent limp and scarring may prejudice her chances with some employers and reduce her range of employment, preventing jobs requiring long periods of standing or walking

comparable_cases.injury_description: degloving injury to both legs and feet; left leg denuded of skin from just below the knee to the ankle exposing muscles and deeper structures; greater part of calf muscle lost
